remediation.title: What Do Animals and Plants Need to Live?

questions.question: Which of these is something ALL living things do?
questions.options: melt | grow | reflect light | stay exactly the same forever
questions.explanation: Every living thing grows — plants, animals and people all start small and get bigger. Melting and reflecting light are things that can happen to non-living objects too.

questions.question: A toy car can move and make sounds. Why is it NOT a living thing?
questions.options: It is too small to be alive | It is made of a hard material | It does not grow, feed or make young | It needs a person to switch it on
questions.correctAnswer: It does not grow, feed or make young
questions.explanation: Moving is not enough to be alive. Living things also grow, need food and water, and make young — a toy car does none of these.

questions.question: Which of these living things can make its own food using sunlight?
questions.options: a goat | a hen | a cat | a mango tree
questions.explanation: Green plants like a mango tree use sunlight, water and air to make their own food. Animals cannot do this — they have to eat plants or other animals.

questions.question: Zahra stirs sand into a cup of water. The sand does not disappear — she can still see the grains. What has she made?
questions.options: a new material | a solution | a mixture | a gas
questions.explanation: When two materials are stirred together but you can still see both of them, that is a mixture. The sand has not dissolved — it is still there.

questions.question: Omar stirs a spoon of salt into warm water until he cannot see it any more. What has happened to the salt?
questions.options: It has melted into a liquid | It has dissolved in the water | It has turned into a gas | It has disappeared forever
questions.correctAnswer: It has dissolved in the water
questions.explanation: The salt has dissolved — its tiny pieces have spread out through the water to make a clear solution. The salt is still there; you could even taste it!

questions.question: Ahmed wants to find out whether sugar dissolves faster in warm water or cold water. To make his test FAIR, what must he keep the same in both cups?
questions.options: the time he waits before looking | nothing — a fair test changes everything | the temperature of the water | the amount of water and sugar
questions.correctAnswer: the amount of water and sugar
questions.explanation: In a fair test you change only ONE thing — here, the water temperature. Everything else, like how much water and sugar he uses, must stay the same in both cups.

questions.question: Which of these is a natural source of light?
questions.options: the Sun | the Moon | a shiny spoon | a mirror
questions.explanation: The Sun makes its own light, so it is a natural light source. Mirrors, the Moon and shiny spoons only bounce light that comes from somewhere else.

questions.question: Layla stands in the sunshine and sees a dark shape on the ground behind her. Why does this shadow form?
questions.options: Light bends around her body | Her body blocks the light | The ground makes its own darkness | The Sun switches off behind her
questions.explanation: Light travels in straight lines. Layla’s body is opaque, so the light cannot pass through her — and the dark space where the light is blocked is her shadow.

questions.question: Which material lets light pass straight through it, so you can see clearly to the other side?
questions.options: thick cardboard | clear glass | a brick | wood
questions.explanation: Clear glass is transparent — light passes straight through it. That is why windows are made of glass. Wood, cardboard and brick are opaque, so light cannot get through.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around your whole body?
questions.options: the lungs | the brain | the heart | the stomach
questions.explanation: Your heart is a strong muscle that squeezes again and again, pushing blood to every part of your body. You can feel it beating in your chest.

questions.question: When you breathe in, which organs fill up with air?
questions.options: the heart | the muscles | the kidneys | the lungs
questions.explanation: Your lungs are like two soft balloons inside your chest. When you breathe in, they fill with air and take the oxygen your body needs.

questions.question: Which part of your skeleton protects your brain?
questions.options: the spine | the skull | the knee bones | the ribs
questions.explanation: The skull is the hard, round case of bone around your head. It works like a helmet, keeping your soft brain safe.

questions.question: A push or a pull that makes something start moving, stop or change direction is called a...
questions.options: material | shadow | sound | force
questions.explanation: Scientists call every push and pull a force. Forces can start things moving, speed them up, slow them down or change their direction.

questions.question: Which of these objects will a magnet attract?
questions.options: a rubber band | an iron nail | a wooden pencil | a plastic spoon
questions.explanation: Magnets attract things made of iron and some other metals. Plastic, wood and rubber are not magnetic, so the magnet will not pull them.

questions.question: Yusuf rolls a ball across the grass. It slows down and stops. Which force slows the ball down?
questions.options: magnetism | friction | electricity | light
questions.explanation: Friction is the force made when two surfaces rub together. The rough grass rubs against the ball and slows it down until it stops.

questions.question: What shape are the Earth, the Sun and the Moon?
questions.options: cubes, like boxes | spheres, like balls | flat circles, like plates | cones, like party hats
questions.explanation: The Earth, the Sun and the Moon are all spheres — round like balls, not flat like plates. That is why the Moon looks like a circle from every side.

questions.question: During the day, the Sun seems to move across the sky. What really causes this?
questions.options: The Sun flies around the Earth | The Earth is spinning | The clouds push the Sun along | The Moon pulls the Sun across the sky
questions.explanation: The Sun is not really moving across our sky — the Earth is spinning round once every 24 hours, which makes the Sun seem to travel from east to west.

questions.question: What does the Moon travel around?
questions.options: nothing — it stays still | the Sun only | the stars | the Earth
questions.explanation: The Moon goes around the Earth — it is our closest neighbour in space. Gravity holds it close so it circles us again and again.

questions.question: What do ALL animals need to stay alive?
questions.options: other animals to play with | food, water and air | toys, beds and houses | sunshine only
questions.explanation: Every animal — big or small — needs food, water and air to live and grow. Homes and friends are nice, but food, water and air keep animals alive.

questions.question: Rocks are natural materials. Where do rocks come from?
questions.options: a factory | the ground | a supermarket | a recycling bin
questions.explanation: Rocks are natural — they come from the ground and were not made by people. Factories make things like plastic, which are man-made materials.

questions.question: Hassan leaves a bar of chocolate in the sunshine and it turns runny. What is this change called?
questions.options: melting | freezing | dissolving | mixing
questions.explanation: When a solid gets warm and turns into a liquid, we call it melting. The warm sunshine melted the solid chocolate into runny chocolate.

questions.question: Which of these makes its own light?
questions.options: a candle flame | a mirror | the Moon | a sheet of white paper
questions.explanation: A candle flame is a light source — it makes its own light. The Moon, mirrors and white paper only bounce back light that comes from somewhere else.

questions.question: Which of these needs electricity to work?
questions.options: a television | a kite | a book | a drum
questions.explanation: A television needs electricity to make its pictures and sound. A book, a drum and a kite all work without any electricity at all.

questions.question: Which of these is SAFE to use in your own science experiments at home?
questions.options: a small battery | a broken plug | a wall socket | a bare electrical wire
questions.explanation: Small batteries hold only a little electricity, so they are safe for experiments. Wall sockets, broken plugs and bare wires carry mains electricity, which is very dangerous — never touch them.

questions.question: The Sun rises in the morning, climbs high, then sets in the evening. When is your shadow SHORTEST?
questions.options: at night | at midday, when the Sun is highest | late in the evening | early in the morning
questions.correctAnswer: at midday, when the Sun is highest
questions.explanation: When the Sun is high above you at midday, your body blocks less light sideways, so your shadow is short. In the morning and evening the Sun is low, and shadows stretch out long.

questions.question: Which of these is alive?
questions.options: a bicycle | a stone | a spoon | a goat
questions.explanation: A goat eats, grows, moves by itself and has baby goats — so it is alive. Stones, spoons and bicycles do none of these things.

questions.question: Which part of a plant grows under the soil and holds the plant in place?
questions.options: the root | the flower | the stem | the leaf
questions.explanation: The roots grow down into the soil. They hold the plant steady, like an anchor, and take in the water the plant needs.

questions.question: Which body part do you use to hear the sound of a drum?
questions.options: your nose | your hands | your eyes | your ears
questions.explanation: You hear with your ears — they catch the sounds around you. Your eyes see, your nose smells and your hands touch.

questions.question: Amina opens a drawer by moving it towards herself. Is that a push or a pull?
questions.options: a pull | a twist | a bounce | a push
questions.explanation: Moving something towards you is a pull. Moving something away from you — like closing the drawer again — is a push.

questions.question: A plant on a windowsill grows tall and green. Which TWO things is it getting that every plant needs?
questions.options: paint and paper | water and light | wind and shadow | sweets and milk
questions.explanation: Plants need water and light to live and grow. A sunny windowsill gives light, and someone waters the pot — that is why the plant is doing so well.
